newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG WIN 1-0, POSTPONE MONACO CELEBRATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG WIN 1-0, POSTPONE MONACO CELEBRATIONS.

text.p: Paris St Germain kept Monaco's French league title celebrations on hold with a 1-0 win at Lille on Wednesday.

Right back Jimmy Algerino headed home in the 14th minute as PSG, showing soundness in defence they will need in the European Cup Winners' Cup final against Barcelona on May 14, reduced Monaco's lead to nine points with three games to go.
Monaco won 2-0 at Strasbourg on Tuesday to virtually take their sixth championship and first since 1988, but PSG retain a slim mathematical chance of overtaking them.
One point from their home game against relegation candidates Caen on Sunday will be enough for Monaco to open the champagne, while the Parisians have a tough match at home to Bordeaux on Saturday.

PSG's full backs combined for the only goal at Lille as Didier Domi sent in a cross from the left and Algerino, coming in from the right, headed over advancing goalkeeper Jean-Marie Aubry and into the net.
Nantes extended their unbeaten run in the league to 28 games with a 3-1 win away against 10-man Nancy to stay in third place three points behind PSG.
Nancy defender Cedric Lecluse was sent off after half an hour for bringing down Japhet N'Doram from behind inside the box.
The striker, who opened the scoring after 20 minutes, converted the penalty for his second goal of the game and 20th in the championship.
Claude Makelele added a third for Nantes shortly after the interval and PSG-bound midfielder Eric Rabesandratana pulled one back for relegation candidates Nancy 15 minutes from time.

Nantes now hold the best and second best unbeaten runs in the French league with a record 32 in a row in their 1994/5 championship season. The third best is PSG's 27 games unbeaten the previous season.
Le Havre greatly eased their relegation worries with a shock 2-1 win away to Bastia that puts the Corsicans UEFA Cup hopes in serious doubt as they have now dropped down to eighth.
Midfielder Nicolas Huysman scored both Le Havre's goals. Striker Sebastian Perez managed to pull one back for Bastia in the final minute.

Veteran former Marseille striker Jean-Pierre Papin was in fine form as he inspired Bordeaux to a 2-1 home win over Lens with a brilliant 22nd-minute equaliser, weaving past three defenders to hit a low shot past 'keeper Guillaume Warmuz.
Bordeaux are now fourth, while Metz climbed two places to fifth -- the lowest of three automatic UEFA Cup places behind the top two who go into the European Cup -- with a 3-1 win at Rennes.
Defending champions Auxerre, 1-0 winners at home to Guingamp with a Bernard Diomede goal directly from a corner, are in seventh, equal on points with Bastia and Lyon.
An early Alain Caveglia penalty, his 17th goal of the season, gave Lyon a 1-0 win at relegated Nice, Guingamp's rivals in the May 10 French Cup final.

Nothing changed in the relegation dogfight except that Nancy and Lille are now six points adrift of Le Havre and Rennes, the teams just above the drop zone, and Caen seven behind with nine points still to play for.
